scope: Isolated interior diagnostics only; no exterior/traversal/fullworld acceptance.

defects: A: Two rows of unsupported wooden blocks float from the floor to the rafters, competing with the trainer and obscuring the desk end of the hall. B removes that conspicuous broken-assembly read.

Both: The end desk and matching bookcases provide a little inhabited context, but shelves have harsh orange scratch-like detail, the banner pair is blank, and the broad cobble floor dominates the composition. Floor and wall stone have similar visual frequency.

Both: The blue coat, white collar, dark trousers and brown backpack give the trainer a readable silhouette; boots lack convincing ground contact/shadow. The large doors and tall windows make the room feel monumental, while small benches look under-scaled within the empty volume.
A: Unsupported blocks remain visible through the haze and interrupt the intended desk focal point. B clears the obstruction but does not recover atmospheric structure.

Both: An almost uniform beige veil turns dark wood and stone pale, while the banners remain strongly blue and windows pure black. This inconsistent separation looks composited rather than like a warm room at night.

Both: A bright circular pool lies in front of the trainer, but his crisp, brightly outlined body and shadowless feet feel suspended over the floor. The desk and shelves disappear at contact-sheet size.
A: Repeated floating block columns dominate the foreground; B has a clear approach to the desk.

Both: Rain mainly changes the room to a slightly duller, warmer grey; the windows supply no readable exterior weather cue or directional overcast-light relationship. An interior need not show rain particles, but weather atmosphere remains weak.

highest_value_fixes.improvement: Restore convincing enclosure and physical grounding.
highest_value_fixes.detail: Use the clear B nave arrangement rather than unsupported A block chains. Resolve the blue triangular/black discontinuities at the far eave joins in reverse and side-night views. Make trainer boot contact and cast shading agree with the floor; retain the disclosed 1.80 m human scale. This is a visual-contact finding, not a traversal or animation judgment.

highest_value_fixes.improvement: Rebuild the interior light hierarchy, especially night.
highest_value_fixes.detail: Reduce the uniform beige veil; preserve dark timber, stone and corners while concentrating warm light around actual lanterns/candles. Give windows a coherent day, overcast and cool-night contribution. Match trainer exposure and atmospheric integration to nearby props. Remove dotted pedestal-edge artifacts and patchy wall glare. Verify both presets separately.

highest_value_fixes.improvement: Give the Hall a designed architectural and shrine identity.
highest_value_fixes.detail: The current rectangular door strips, repeated blank windows and identical angled lecterns cannot communicate eight destinations by silhouette. Author coherent portal surrounds, legible biome emblems and purpose-built pedestal/relic shapes; use thicker structural supports, varied stone scale and restrained material detail. Then stage existing benches, storage and desk props as usable human-scale clusters, leaving clear circulation. New art means authored shapes/materials, not necessarily acquired assets; wholesale trainer replacement is not established by rear-only stills.

bar_a_world_fit_rationale: NO for A; NO for B at the stated keyart-world-fit bar. B is clearly preferable in nave frames because unsupported block chains are absent. Natural stone, cream plaster, brown timber, blue fabric and the blue-coated backpacked trainer are compatible ingredients, and the shrine candle corners give a modest cozy cue. Yet the empty institutional volume, mechanical repetition, weak shrine/portal silhouettes and overwhelmingly grey cobble surfaces do not deliver the keyart intent of an authored, inviting inhabited world. This judges palette, mood, composition and silhouette rather than painted-pixel fidelity. The trainer art has a readable blue/white/brown design, recognizable spiky hair and backpack, but small-size detail becomes noisy and night lighting/contact make him look composited. Rear views cannot establish facial appeal. The fixed 1.80 m scale is broadly plausible against doors and lecterns; architecture needs better human-scale subdivisions and contact evidence rather than arbitrary character resizing. All 26 full-size pairs and the contact sheet were inspected. Medium and High receive the same numeric scores where visible differences do not change the judgment.
bar_b_atmosphere_rationale: NO for A; NO for B for shipping Palworld/Valheim presentation. Same kind of game as Palworld: NO on the visual evidence of this isolated hall, although the third-person adventurer silhouette and rustic fantasy props are genre-compatible. The broad material variation, convincing subject/environment contact, designed focal shapes and depth seen in the Palworld references are absent here; no gameplay-type inference is claimed. Day is readable but flat and repetitive, rain is only a modest tonal shift, and night is a severe beige wash with solid-black windows, disconnected floor glows and an incongruously crisp trainer. B fixes an obvious nave artifact, not commercial atmosphere. Shrine arms are effectively tied. Scope remains isolated Hall interior with a fixed idle trainer: no exterior, fullworld, traversal, continuous-motion or performance acceptance is inferred.
